text.title: Ads Attribution Models Core Rules
text.summary: 16 testable rules every application of Ads Attribution Models MUST enforce — warehouse truth, 15% variance threshold, quarterly geo-holdout, weekly variance report, frozen definitions, model selection by sales cycle, documented platform defaults, lookback windows, locked source of truth, 4-week incrementality tests, human sign-off thresholds, offline-conversion hashing. Rationale + source per rule. Rules referenced by id from `content/06-decision-tree.xml`.

section.title: Background
section.p: When a user clicks a Meta ad then a Google ad before purchasing, both platforms record the conversion. Platform totals routinely exceed actual sales by 20-40%.

section.title: Rule set

rule.statement: Warehouse MUST be the canonical source of truth. Platforms are inputs.
rule.rationale: Platforms double-count and use different windows; only warehouse can dedup across sources.

rule.statement: Variance > 15% between platform / GA4 / warehouse MUST trigger investigation before budget decisions.
rule.rationale: Above 15% indicates pixel misfire, dedup failure, or definition drift; acting on bad data destroys budget.

rule.statement: Quarterly geo-holdout incrementality test MUST run per major channel. Without it, true incremental lift is unknown.

rationale.source: Incrementality testing literature — Wieczorek, Air Force/Google

rule.rationale: Attribution models estimate share-of-credit; only incrementality tests measure true lift.

rule.statement: Variance report MUST run weekly with named reviewer. Monthly is too slow to catch pixel drift.
rule.rationale: Pixel breakage often surfaces within days; weekly cadence catches it before quarter-end damage.

rule.statement: Conversion definitions (event name, window, dedup key) MUST be frozen quarterly. Mid-quarter changes invalidate comparisons.
rule.rationale: Definition drift mid-quarter generates apparent variance that is actually a definition artifact.

section.p: Defines the six attribution models, explains the cross-platform overlap problem, and provides lookback window guidelines by sales cycle length.

rule.statement: Select an attribution model based on sales cycle length and available conversion volume, not platform convenience.
rule.rationale: Each model assigns credit differently and will produce different CPA and ROAS numbers for the same spend. Using the wrong model leads to systematically over- or under-investing in channels.

rule.statement: Document the attribution model and lookback window for every platform in use; never assume defaults are consistent across platforms.

rationale.source: Meta / Google Ads / GA4 attribution settings docs

rule.rationale: Each platform uses different defaults: Meta counts 7-day click + 1-day view, Google Ads uses last Google click at 30 days, GA4 uses data-driven at 90 days. Comparing numbers without knowing this is meaningless.

rule.statement: Use GA4 or a warehouse-deduped view as the single source of truth for cross-channel performance; use platform data only for in-platform optimization.
rule.rationale: GA4 deduplicates across channels using the same user session. Platform data remains useful for optimizing bids and creative within that platform's ecosystem.

rule.statement: Match lookback window to actual sales cycle; never use a shorter window to make numbers look better.
rule.rationale: A 7-day window on a 30-day SaaS trial cycle will miss the majority of attributed conversions and undercount channel contribution.

section.p: Choosing a unified source of truth, configuring GA4 and platform attribution settings, and running geo-holdout incrementality tests.

rule.statement: Pick one attribution source of truth (usually GA4 data-driven or warehouse on top of GA4 export) and apply it consistently across all budget decisions.
rule.rationale: Switching models mid-flight invalidates historical comparisons and causes confusion during budget reviews. A documented, locked model is more valuable than the theoretically best model.

rule.statement: Run a geo-holdout incrementality test at least once per quarter when spending $10k+/month to validate the attribution model.
rule.rationale: Data-driven attribution drifts over time and cannot detect true causal lift. A geo-holdout measures actual revenue lift vs. a control region, providing ground truth that no model can replicate.

rule.statement: Run incrementality tests for at least 4 weeks and do not change budgets or targeting during the test period.
rule.rationale: Short tests produce noise, not signal. Budget changes mid-test contaminate the treatment-control comparison and invalidate results.

section.p: Concrete rules for agents building attribution pipelines, including variance thresholds, human-in-loop checkpoints, and failure modes specific to LLM agents.

rule.statement: Always present three numbers per channel (platform-reported, GA4-modeled, warehouse-deduped) and flag if any two diverge by more than 15%.
rule.rationale: Below 15% variance is noise. Above 15% indicates a structural issue — mismatched windows, missing dedup key, or a tracking gap — that must be investigated before budget decisions.

rule.statement: Require human sign-off before any budget reallocation exceeding 10% of total spend, any change to the canonical attribution model, or any retroactive re-attribution.
rule.rationale: These actions have irreversible consequences: retroactive re-attribution destroys audit trail, model changes invalidate historical comparisons, and large reallocations cannot be easily undone.

rule.statement: When uploading offline conversions, SHA-256 hash lowercase-trimmed email addresses before sending; verify match rate is above 30% before declaring the upload successful.

rationale.source: Google Ads / Meta offline conversion docs

rule.rationale: Agents that skip email normalization (lowercase + trim) see near-zero match rates silently. A match rate below 30% indicates a normalization or hashing bug.

rule.statement: If applicability preconditions are unmet (see AGENTS.md Skip If), the methodology MUST be skipped and a one-line skip-reason logged.
rule.rationale: A named skip terminal keeps decision-tree leaves resolvable and prevents silent misuse on misfit inputs.
